newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan consensus-building forum faces split.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan consensus-building forum faces split.

text.p: An all-party conference aimed to build consensus and sketch out a grand blueprint for Taiwan's future received a major blow on Friday when a key opposition party announced it would no longer take part in the forum.
The fledgling New Party accused the ruling Nationalist Party of manipulating the National Development Conference and of refusing to compromise.
"Our opinions did not receive proper attention and respect. We feel we have no choice but to withdraw," New Party leader Chen Kuei-miao told reporters.

The New Party divided sharply with the ruling party on political reforms, including a proposal to abolish or marginalise Taiwan's provincial government, and said it did not want to endorse the Nationalists' package.
The ruling Nationalist Party and leading opposition Democratic Progressive Party expressed their regret about the New Party's withdrawal but vowed to continue the meeting.
"We have tried our best to make all parties stay in the conference until the end," Wu Poh-hsiung, secretary-general of the ruling Nationalist Party, said.
"We are very sorry about the New Party's withdrawal."
Hsu Hsin-liang, chairman of the Democratic Progressive Party said: "The New Party's withdrawal will not affect our position and presence in the National Development Conference."

President Lee Teng-hui proposed the all-party conference during his May 20 inaugural address and a hopeful sponsoring government has said it believed some common ground could be discovered during the ambitious December 23-28 meeting.

On the agenda for the week-long forum are constitutional reforms and party politics, economic development and relations between Taiwan and communist China, the island's giant neighbour and sometimes-menacing diplomatic arch rival.
Participants include senior officials, party and business leaders, investors, academics and other Taiwan elites.
"We welcome our friends at the New Party to return to the meeting and join our discussion at any time," Huang Kun-huei, President Lee's chief of staff, said.
